neighbours.label: the closing word of a few fixed expressions built from function words ('can-do', 'to the max', 'by the numbers', 'to within'), not the same words in ordinary use
fire: The new manager brought a can-do attitude to the struggling team.
For the party they decorated the hall to the max with lights.
The inspector did everything strictly by the numbers that day.
The clock is accurate to within a second per year.
Volunteers with a can-do spirit rebuilt the playground in a weekend.
Her summer was packed to the max with trips and concerts.
The magazine runs a monthly column called By the Numbers.
The laser can align the parts to within a hair's width.
quiet: The new manager said the team can do better than last season.
For the party they set the heater to its max setting.
The inspector added up all the numbers on the invoice that day.
The clock sits within a small glass case in the hall.
Volunteers said they can do the repairs in a weekend.
Her summer schedule had a max of two trips abroad.
The magazine prints the lottery numbers every Monday.
The laser sits within a sealed metal box.

predictions: 6/8 fire; ordinary uses of can, max, numbers and within below 0.1.
short: closing word of can-do / to the max
notes: Card: peaks '-do' in can-do, '-max' in to-the-max, 'bers' in by-the-numbers, ' Numbers' in By The Numbers, ' within' in 'to within'. Probe: can-do 0.952, pimped-to-the-max 0.739, by-the-numbers 0.545, "By the Numbers" 0.564, 'to within a few microns' 0.461, 'Please can I' 0.402; never-say-die 0.016, well-known 0.005. A list of set phrases, not a general rule: never-say-die did not fire.
